subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In the ideal gas equation pV = nRT, the temperature T must be measured in:
questions.explain: pV = nRT requires the absolute (Kelvin) temperature.

questions.q: For a simple pendulum of length L, the period of small oscillations is:
questions.explain: The simple pendulum period is T = 2π√(L/g).

questions.q: In kinetic theory, the duration of collisions between gas molecules is assumed to be:
options: Long compared to time between collisions
Equal to the time between collisions
Negligible compared to time between collisions
questions.explain: Collision times are assumed negligible compared with the time between collisions.

questions.q: The specific heat capacity equation is:
questions.explain: Energy to change temperature is Q = mcΔT.

questions.q: The angular speed ω of an object completing one revolution in period T is:
questions.explain: One revolution is 2π radians, so ω = 2π/T.

questions.q: The mean kinetic energy of a molecule in an ideal gas is given by:
questions.explain: Mean translational kinetic energy per molecule is (3/2)kT.

questions.q: When two objects are in thermal equilibrium, they have the same:
questions.explain: Thermal equilibrium means no net heat flow, which occurs when temperatures are equal.

questions.q: For circular motion, which expression for centripetal acceleration uses angular speed ω?
questions.explain: Since v = ωr, the acceleration v²/r equals ω²r.

questions.q: Absolute zero is best defined as the temperature at which:
options: All motion of every kind ceases entirely
Particles have minimum internal energy and zero kinetic energy on average
Pressure of any gas is at its maximum
questions.explain: At absolute zero particles have minimum internal energy; their average kinetic energy is zero.

questions.q: At the equilibrium position in SHM, the energy is:
questions.explain: At equilibrium displacement is zero so PE is minimum and KE is maximum.

questions.q: The defining equation for simple harmonic motion is:
questions.explain: In SHM, acceleration is proportional to displacement and directed opposite to it: a = −ω²x.

questions.q: During SHM, total mechanical energy (in the absence of damping):
options: Stays constant as KE and PE interchange
questions.explain: Total energy is constant; kinetic and potential energy interchange throughout the cycle.

questions.q: A heavily (over) damped system, when displaced and released:
options: Returns to equilibrium very slowly without oscillating
questions.explain: Heavy damping causes a slow return to equilibrium with no oscillation.

questions.q: Why does the centripetal force do no work on an object in uniform circular motion?
options: Speed is constant so energy is conserved automatically
The force is perpendicular to the velocity
questions.explain: The centripetal force points toward the centre, perpendicular to the velocity, so it does no work.

questions.q: A fixed mass of gas at 2.0 × 10⁵ Pa and 300 K is heated at constant volume to 600 K. The new pressure is:
questions.explain: At constant volume p ∝ T, so doubling T doubles p to 4.0 × 10⁵ Pa.

questions.q: In the equation pV = nRT, the quantity n represents:
questions.explain: n is the number of moles; R is the molar gas constant.

questions.q: The internal energy of a system is the sum of:
options: The random kinetic and potential energies of all particles
Only the potential energies of the particles
The ordered kinetic energy of the whole body
Only the kinetic energies of the particles
questions.explain: Internal energy is the total of the random kinetic and potential energies of the particles.

questions.q: Which is NOT an assumption of the kinetic theory of an ideal gas?
options: Molecules exert strong attractive forces on each other except during collisions
Molecules are in continuous random motion
The volume of molecules is negligible compared with the gas volume
questions.explain: Kinetic theory assumes negligible intermolecular forces except during collisions, not strong ones.

questions.q: Temperature is a measure of the:
options: Average random kinetic energy of the particles
Total internal energy of a body
questions.explain: Absolute temperature is proportional to the average random kinetic energy of particles.

questions.q: The kinetic theory equation is pV = ⅓Nm⟨c²⟩, where ⟨c²⟩ is the:
questions.explain: ⟨c²⟩ is the mean square speed of the molecules.

questions.q: The velocity in SHM as a function of displacement x is v = ±ω√(A²−x²). At equilibrium (x=0), the speed is:
questions.explain: At x = 0 the speed is maximum, equal to ωA.

questions.q: The Boltzmann constant k is related to the molar gas constant R by:
questions.explain: The Boltzmann constant k = R/N_A, the gas constant per molecule.

questions.q: In SHM, the maximum speed of an oscillator of amplitude A is:
questions.explain: Maximum speed v_max = ωA, occurring at the equilibrium position.

questions.q: Heating a gas at constant pressure causes it to expand. The work done is by the gas, so its internal energy change for a given heat input Q is:
questions.explain: Some heat does work in expansion, so the internal energy increase is less than Q.

questions.q: A car rounds a flat curve. The force providing the centripetal force is:
questions.explain: On a flat road, friction between the tyres and road supplies the centripetal force.

questions.q: A system that returns to equilibrium in the shortest time without oscillating is:
questions.explain: Critical damping returns the system to equilibrium fastest without overshooting.

questions.q: Specific latent heat is the energy needed to change the state of:
options: 1 kg of substance at constant temperature
questions.explain: Specific latent heat is the energy per kilogram to change state at constant temperature.

questions.q: The specific latent heat of vaporisation is generally larger than that of fusion because:
options: Gases have higher specific heat capacity
Separating particles fully and doing work against the atmosphere needs more energy
Vaporisation occurs at a higher temperature
questions.explain: Vaporisation requires breaking nearly all intermolecular bonds and work against the atmosphere.

questions.q: Light damping causes the amplitude of free oscillations to:
questions.explain: With light damping the amplitude decays exponentially while oscillation continues.

questions.q: A real gas behaves most like an ideal gas at:
questions.explain: At low pressure and high temperature molecules are far apart with negligible interactions.
